versions.short: The bill would stop the U.S. Treasury from producing new pennies for everyday circulation, except to meet the needs of coin collectors, while keeping the penny legal money. It would require cash payments and transfers, such as sales and cash wages, to be rounded up or down to an amount divisible by five. The bill would also let Treasury stop minting any coin for circulation if it follows set procedures, including notifying and briefing Congress. It would require the Federal Reserve Board to report periodically on a plan for accepting penny orders and deposits at commercial coin terminals. Finally, it would allow the nickel to be made from a different material, a zinc core with a nickel outer layer, in addition to the current copper-nickel alloy.
